skill.name: adapt
skill.description: Adapt helps redesign interfaces for different devices, screen sizes, input methods, platforms, and channels while preserving usable core workflows.
skill.summary: Guides context-aware interface adaptation for responsive, print, email, and cross-device experiences.
skill.author: pbakaus

content.value_statement: Teams often lose usability when moving a design to another device or channel. This skill guides context-aware layout, interaction, content, navigation, and testing decisions.
actual_capabilities: Identifies assumptions behind the current design, including screen size, input method, connection, and usage context.
Recommends mobile, tablet, desktop, print, and email adaptation strategies.
Guides layout, interaction, content, and navigation changes for each context.
Suggests responsive techniques such as grid, flexbox, container queries, media queries, and fluid sizing.
Lists verification checks across devices, orientations, browsers, operating systems, input methods, and slow connections.
limitations: It provides guidance and checklists; it does not run device tests automatically.
It depends on details the user provides about the source and target context.
It does not replace accessibility, performance, or usability testing with real users.
It does not generate production code without additional implementation prompts.

use_cases.title: Adapt Product Screens
use_cases.description: Turn a desktop product screen into a usable mobile or tablet experience.

use_cases.title: Plan Responsive Implementation
use_cases.description: Map layout, content, and interaction changes before writing responsive interface code.

use_cases.title: Review Cross-Channel Designs
use_cases.description: Check whether web experiences can work in print, email, and device-specific contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt One Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single interface element.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product card and adapt it for mobile. Focus on layout, touch targets, navigation, and content priority.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Tablet Layouts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for tablet-specific design planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a tablet adaptation plan for this desktop dashboard. Include portrait and landscape differences.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt Across Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this web checkout flow for email and print contexts. List layout, content, and testing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Multi-Platform Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for a full cross-platform review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature for mobile, tablet, desktop, and print. Identify assumptions, risks, and a testing matrix.

output_examples.input: Adapt a desktop analytics dashboard for mobile.
output: Prioritize the key metric and latest alerts first.
Move secondary filters into a bottom sheet.
Use a single-column layout with large touch controls.
Test portrait, landscape, slow connections, and touch navigation.

output_examples.input: Adapt a marketing page for email.
output: Keep the main call to action clear and visible.
Test in major email clients before launch.

output_examples.input: Review a mobile flow for desktop users.
output: Use the wider screen for persistent navigation and supporting panels.
Show more context upfront without overwhelming the primary task.

best_practices: Start by naming the original assumptions before choosing breakpoints.
Adapt interaction patterns for the active input method, not only for screen width.
Validate changes on real devices, orientations, browsers, and slow connections.
anti_patterns: Do not hide core functionality on mobile when users still need it.
Do not use generic breakpoints when content breaks earlier or later.
Do not rely on hover behavior for touch-first interfaces.

faq.question: What does this skill adapt?
faq.answer: It adapts interface designs for mobile, tablet, desktop, print, email, and other contexts.

faq.question: Can it create production code?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation choices, but final production code needs a separate development prompt.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights touch targets, input methods, readable text, and testing across devices.

faq.question: Can it help with email designs?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends narrow layouts, inline styling constraints, simple calls to action, and compatibility testing.

faq.question: How should I provide context?
faq.answer: Share the current design, target platform, user goals, constraints, and known issues.

faq.question: Does it replace device testing?
faq.answer: No. It explicitly recommends real device testing because emulation can miss hardware and browser differences.
